issue.title: Reinstate the whole-system AXE status view as sase scheduler status --full
issue.description: Operator view of the full scheduler snapshot lost when sase axe status became an alias of sase scheduler status.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Reinstate the whole-system AXE status view, for example as `sase scheduler status --full` (plus `-j/--json`).

Proposed by sase-11y.10.1.3.1.5 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1), per the epic plan's "Two decisions this plan makes" section. Epic sase-11y.10.1.3.1 made `sase axe status` an alias of `sase scheduler status`, which prints the `scheduler` service proc's show view. With that change, `src/sase/axe/status_render.py` (`render_axe_status_human` / `render_axe_status_json`) lost its only consumer and was deleted in b87c8e3ee. That removed the only CLI surface for the rich snapshot: routine tree, runner occupancy, maintenance, lifecycle events, and classified issues.

The data survives: `collect_axe_status_snapshot` (`src/sase/axe/status_collector.py`) still feeds `sase doctor` through `src/sase/doctor/checks_deep_axe.py`. A `--full` flag on `sase scheduler status` could render it again. The deleted renderer is at `git show b87c8e3ee^:src/sase/axe/status_render.py`, and its tests are in the same commit. Keep `sase axe status` a pure alias, so the flag lands on both spellings through the shared `add_json_flag` / parser builders in `src/sase/main/parser_scheduler.py`, and follow the cli_rules memory.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The epic's scope was deletion only ("this plan deletes, it does not add"), and it deliberately aligned `sase axe status` with `sase scheduler status` so the alias behaves identically. Adding a new view is a product decision for the owner, not remaining epic work, and nothing is broken without it: `sase doctor` still reports the same classified issues.
